title: Quarter Past Twelve in Almeria
subject: A stunt gunfighter at a tourist western town in the Almería desert has been shot dead at the same balcony every day at 12:15 for twenty-two years; today a small child in the crowd claps for him alone.
caption: Cinematic spaghetti-western ballad, slow 4/4 pulse with a heartbeat kick. Nylon-string and twangy tremolo electric guitar playing a slow arpeggio, a solo whistle carrying the melody, a harmonica answering, a sweeping string section with low cello, and rolling timpani with a distant church bell. Wide 1968 Rome studio texture, spacious desert reverb, spring reverb on guitar, dry intimate vocal. Male lead, deep warm baritone, low-mid register, slow and weathered, with a small male choir humming softly on the chorus. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 70 BPM, D minor. Dusty, solemn, quietly proud. No drum machine, no synth pads, no autotune, no rock drum kit, no modern pop beat.
lyrics:
[Intro - whistle over tremolo guitar, timpani heartbeat]

[Verse 1]
Noon in Almería, the tourists come
Sit on the rail with ice cream and drum
I put on the hat and the dusty black coat
Check the cap gun, check the rope

[Chorus]
Quarter past twelve, the shot goes off
I spin, I stagger, I give a cough
They clap for the hero, they clap for the pay
Nobody claps for the man who stays

[Verse 2]
A crack in the plank where my shoulder lands
Sand in my collar, sand in my hands
My knees say no, my pride says yes
Twenty-two years in the same black vest

[Pre-Chorus]
Today a small boy in a paper hat
Stands on a bench, says "Look at that"
He doesn't clap for the man with the gun
He claps for me, the fallen one

[Chorus]
Quarter past twelve, the shot goes off
I spin, I stagger, I give a cough
One little pair of hands, one little sound
Tells a dead man he's still around

[Bridge - strings swell, whistle alone]
I lie in the dust with my hat on my chest
And for once I do not want to rest

[Outro - whistle and harmonica, strings fade, bell]
Quarter past twelve
Quarter past twelve
